prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
By September 2026, Japan’s travel data shows a clear tension. Young people, especially young men, are showing more interest in traveling at their own pace. But the stays measured in surveys are still short. The story is not that sightseeing has already been replaced by long, slow holidays. It is that the wish is moving faster than the behavior.

In a 2025 survey, men aged 29 and under placed solo travel and hobby-focused travel near the top. Each was chosen by about one in four respondents. Another survey found that about 90% of Japanese Gen Z respondents wanted free time during an overseas tour. About 80% of them wanted at least half a day.

The picture changes when people imagine having more time. When asked how long they would travel with a month off, the most common answer was about one week, chosen by about 24%. But another autumn survey of people planning domestic trips found shorter plans: an average of 1.8 nights, with a median of about 2 nights.

This is why the trend needs careful wording. The desire for freedom and a slower pace is visible across several surveys. Yet longer stays are still described as a policy task. For now, young travelers may be changing what they want from a trip before they are changing how long they stay.

【Point One】
A short trip is not automatically a fast trip. When about nine in ten young respondents want free time inside a tour, and about eight in ten of them want half a day or more, the first sign of this travel mood may be the schedule, not the number of nights. Even a two-night stay can include time chosen by the traveler. Travel planners may need to build that choice into short packages.

【Point Two】
The data do not describe one new youth style. Among men aged 29 and under, solo travel and hobby-focused trips were each chosen by about one in four. For women of the same age, visiting famous tourist sites remained popular at about 45%. A single “youth travel” message could miss this split: one group may respond to personal interests, while another still wants famous sights.

point_one.reasoning: Full Storyの短期滞在と自由時間への希望というデータを、宿泊日数ではなく旅行中のスケジュール設計が変化の初期兆候になり得るという解釈に発展させている。さらに、短期パッケージにも旅行者が選べる時間を組み込むべきだという具体的な示唆を加えている。

point_two.reasoning: 若い男性のソロ旅行・趣味重視に加え、同年代女性では有名観光地が人気という性別差を示し、単一の「若者向け」施策では需要を取りこぼす可能性を説明している。Full Storyにはなかった具体的なセグメント分けとメッセージ設計への示唆があり、新しい価値を加えている。
